(b) reservation of the offices shall be made when

Block, as the case may be, matches the number

ignoring the unmatched numbers until the

(vi) If following the principle of rotation, any office is
selected in any term of election simultaneously for
reservation for the Scheduled Tribes, the Scheduled
Castes and the Backward Classes persons or any
two of such categories, such office shall be reserved
in the preferential order of the Scheduled Tribes,
the Scheduled Castes and the Backward Classes
and reservation for the left out Scheduled Castes or
Backward Classes or both, as the case may be, shall
be made out of the offices coming next in order:
Provided that the office so reserved for the
Scheduled Tribes or the Scheduled Castes on the
aforesaid ground shall be eligible for consideration
for reservation for the Scheduled Castes or the
Backward Classes, as the case may be, in the next
term of election.
(vii) If, in a district, the number of the Grams or the
Blocks available for reservation by rotation, falls
short of the number determined under clause (a)
of sub-rule (1), the 1[Commission] may, by order,
include, for the purpose of reservation, such other
offices relating to the Grams or the Blocks, as
the case may be, as have the Scheduled Castes
